title: Upstream defect handoff artifact
description: Shape of evidence/upstream-defects/<owner>__<name>/<fingerprint>.json: an evidence-backed, precise handoff for a human to file, describing one confirmed defect in a target repository's own manifest or source, not a repository-presenter presentation gap (docs/investigations/03-issue-tracking.md section 5). This is a pure read-only-boundary artifact: it carries no GitHub Issues write capability and authorizes no automated filing. causal_stage is pinned to EXTRACTING because validation/registry.py's own repair routing (repair/targeted.py STATE_STAGES) already proves that stage structurally unrepairable by revising the candidate's prose - the one mechanical signal this codebase already has for 'about the target repository, not about our own composition' (investigation section 3). triggering_check.id names either a validation.json blocking check (e.g. BC-02) or, for a repository that never reaches candidate composition at all (a NOT_PROCESSABLE disposition, e.g. unparseable source), the disposition value itself - the repo-level parallel the investigation names in section 3 and section 5. evidence entries are populated only with reproductions run outside repository-presenter's own pipeline (a literal curl, pip install, ast.parse, or gh api observation), never a restatement of the pipeline's own polarity label alone (investigation section 3). suggested_issue_title/suggested_issue_body are literal text a human pastes unmodified into gh issue create; nothing in this schema or the artifacts it governs performs that call.

defect_fingerprint.description: sha256 of {repository, triggering_check.id, a primary-evidence signature}, the stable dedup key of investigation section 4.1 - the same value embeddable as an HTML-comment marker in a filed issue body.

id.description: validation/registry.py Check.id (e.g. BC-02) when a blocking check fired, or the repository-level disposition value (e.g. NOT_PROCESSABLE) when the repository never reached candidate composition.

version.description: The check's Check.version at the time it fired (validation/registry.py), or "1" for a repository-level disposition with no independent versioning of its own.

causal_stage.description: Always EXTRACTING: repair/targeted.py's STATE_STAGES maps only INVESTIGATING/RECONCILING/PLANNING/COMPOSING to a revisable stage, so EXTRACTING is this codebase's own mechanical proof the defect is about the target repository, never the candidate's prose (investigation section 3).

path.description: A target-repository file path, a registry/API URL, or the literal command that produced this observation.

claim.description: One plain factual sentence: what the evidence proves, no severity adjective, no fix claim (idea.md's own seed-example prose style).

suggested_issue_body.description: Literal text a human can paste unmodified into `gh issue create --body-file -`.
